The test image shows a soybean leaf with:
- Large irregular brown/dark lesions scattered across the leaf
- Tan/light brown centers with darker brown-black margins
- Lesions coalescing into larger blotches
- Leaf mostly green between spots
- Some angular appearance to lesions

Top candidates: Septoria_brown_spot, Bacterial_Blight, Frogeye_leaf_spot, Downy_mildew. Let me check references.

The Septoria reference shows small scattered brown spots on yellowed leaves — different. Bacterial Blight shows small angular water-soaked lesions — possible but small. Frogeye shows circular spots with distinct margins — not matching. Let me check more candidates.
Downy mildew shows pale/grayish diffuse areas, Brown Stem Rot shows interveinal yellowing, Cercospora shows dark purple dense spots. None match well. Let me check more candidates.

Key observations from references:
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Interveinal chlorosis with green veins — doesn't match
- **Phyllosticta_leaf_spot**: Bottom-left shows irregular dark brown patches coalescing on green leaf — closer match, but spots appear smaller and more discrete

Re-examining the test image: Large irregular tan/brown lesions with very dark (almost black) margins, some angular/vein-bounded, multiple coalescing lesions on an otherwise green leaf. This angular pattern bounded by veins is the hallmark of **Bacterial_Blight**.

The Bacterial_Blight reference showed early/small lesions, but at advanced stages they coalesce into the larger patches seen in the test image. The dark margins with tan centers and angular vein-bounded pattern is the key distinguishing feature.
